name: Variational Isotropic Meshing
definition: A two-phase method to compute high-quality meshes from an implicit surface S (2-manifold) in domain Ω ⊂ R^3. Phase 1 builds an initial homeomorphic mesh via Delaunay refinement. Phase 2 optimizes the mesh via relaxation to improve sample distribution and approximation quality.
summary: Variational Isotropic Meshing generates high-quality triangular meshes from implicit surfaces by combining Delaunay refinement with a variational relaxation phase that optimizes vertex positions via Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation.
